text:
Jess: Dropping a new variant in Figma: stream-by-sentence instead of char-by-char. Idea is fewer layout updates but still feels live. https://www.figma.com/file/xxxx/playground-stream-sentence

Mike: Interesting. Sentence-level streaming could hide incremental thoughts though. Users sometimes want to copy mid-sentence.

Alana: Could do hybrid: stream sentences but flush partial words on pause. Or expose a "Snapshot" action that takes the current partial output and makes it selectable.

Sam: Snapshot sounds good. UX: small pill "Snapshot" next to Pause. Snapshot freezes current text into a node you can copy/export; generation continues into a new pane below.

Priya: Accessibility: snapshot must be announced to AT with role=status and include a clear label like "Snapshot created: partial response available". Also ensure focus management moves to the snapshot region if user hits some shortcut.

Ravi: Dev constraints: snapshot should be client-only state to avoid extra runtime calls. We can keep the KV cache live and stream continues; snapshot is just a DOM copy. Tradeoff: memory vs network.

Mike: Another engineering point: if we support resume after snapshot, we need to avoid re-sending input. We'll maintain a resume diff token pointer.

Jess: Token budgeting idea: allow user to set a per-message budget (slider: 128/256/512) with inline estimate. Default respects account quota. Show remaining tokens in the chat header per session too.

Alana: Microcopy: slider label should be "Generation length" not "Max tokens" to be more user-friendly. Tooltip: "Approximate output size; model may vary."

Sam: For the token counter UI, propose two lines: small muted text "Session: 12.3k / 50k tokens" and bold when active generation "This run: 42 tokens (est)". Keep contrast high for readability.

Priya: Hotkey discussion: common patterns are `Ctrl+Enter` to send, `Shift+Enter` newline. For rerun, maybe `Alt+R`. Need to document and make configurable in Preferences.

Ravi: Backend: we can emit incremental token estimates with each chunk. We'll add a lightweight event with fields: run_id, estimated_tokens, consumed_tokens. Frontend can smooth spikes.

UX-Bot: A11y reminder: use `aria-live=\"polite\"` for non-critical updates, and `aria-atomic=true` for snapshot announcements. Also ensure color-only token indicators have text equivalents.

Mike: About stop vs finalize: Stop should cancel the stream request. Finalize should both cancel and mark the node as read-only. Users need both.

Jess: UI states: Streaming (live pulse), Paused (resume available), Stopped/Finalized (copy icon shown). We'll sketch a compact and expanded control set. Compact used in inbox view.

Alana: Prompt library flow: when inserting a prompt with placeholders, show a small inline form above the input: fillables rendered as chips (e.g., {topic}, {audience}). Offer "Preview" that shows the prompt with variables substituted.

Sam: Also add a tiny badge on the sent message: "used template" with hover to view template metadata. Helps attribution.

Priya: Contrast & keyboard: ensure all controls reachable by tab; snapshots and finalize actions get clear keyboard labels. For screen reader, add role=button and aria-labels that include state: "Pause stream, currently streaming".

Ravi: Performance: sentence-level streaming reduces DOM ops but requires sentence boundary detection. We'll reuse tokenizer heuristics; still need to fallback to char streaming for weird tokens.

Jess: Will mock three examples: char-stream, sentence-stream, and hybrid snapshot flow. Can folks review by tomorrow 11am?

Mike: I'll prototype the token estimate events and a lightweight sliding average to prevent jitter.

Alana: I'll draft the microcopy options: Snapshot vs Save Draft vs Capture. Will post A/B copy tests in thread.

Sam: Add analytics: track SnapshotCreated, Pause, Resume, Finalize, RerunFromEdit. Include token counts and whether prompt template used.

Priya: I'll run keyboard walkthrough and a small NVDA/VoiceOver test matrix.

Jess: Great. Plan: iterate Figma -> small dev spike -> internal playtest. If snapshot performs well, we prefer sentence/hybrid for first rollout. :rocket:

UX-Bot: Note: file a docs checkbox for Playground keyboard shortcuts and Prompt Library preview behavior.

Mike: One more thing: mobile behavior. On iOS, snapshot action should live under overflow menu to avoid accidental taps. Also compact controls for small screens.

Jess: OK all, thanks! Leaving notes on the Figma frames. We'll reconvene after reviews. End thread.
